rewrites.2ADAA706: Latent interest is not what holds Goal 1 back; converting it into visits is. Six barriers stand between the interested traveller and the trip. Each objective in this goal answers at least one of them.
rewrites.50F3A77A: Travellers struggle to find the province beyond Cape Town on the platforms they use, so regional itineraries, transfers and practical information lead. Regional rooms are listed online. A discovery-to-sale audit shows where product fails to be found or sold.
rewrites.21465511: Goal 1 sets out to break through three ceilings on demand, in markets, seasons and spread, by reshaping the brand towards new traveller segments. Five markets supplied 63% of overseas arrivals in 2025. The UK, Germany and the USA supplied 52% between them. June held 6.4% of the year's international seats at Cape Town International in 2025, against 10.8% in December. Beyond the core routes, named experiences reach the visitor through day tours, walk-ins and local permits more often than through an online ticket.[^246]
rewrites.223A3662: The gap between interest and arrival is wide. About 97 million high-value travellers in 34 markets have an interest in South Africa. About 1.4 million arrive. Six barriers hold conversion back (section 2.1). Goal 1 answers four of them directly and works with Goals 2 and 3 on the other two, as Table 3.2 shows.[^247]
rewrites.6F5FF0A1: Each of the six barriers to conversion has at least one objective that answers it and four of the six are answered inside Goal 1.
rewrites.2AF06F4A: The two themes work as one. The segments set the target inside each market. The market groups set where volume and value come from. The green season and regional information decide whether the demand they win lands in the months and places with room to take it. Initiatives I1 to I5 carry the six objectives and section 4.3 sets out each one.
rewrites.2C7186D3: Four traveller segments, each concentrated in named home markets, give Wesgro a sharper target than country alone and the province scores 3.7 to 4.6 out of 5 on its ability to win them.
rewrites.3FCC081D: Country is too blunt a target for a long-haul destination. Within one market, travellers differ in what they want from a trip, what they spend and where they book. Four values-based segments fit the Western Cape. Together they hold about 97 million addressable travellers. Each is concentrated in named home markets. Marketing to a segment inside a market puts each rand where the province is most likely to win.[^249]
rewrites.11601E80: The prize to 2035 is value as much as volume. Curious Explorers and Creative Connectors together hold over 40% of global outbound leisure demand, while Discerning Connoisseurs deliver the highest economic impact per arrival. The segments also help with season and spread. Curious Explorers offer the strongest opportunity for dispersal beyond Cape Town. Reflective Adventurers support seasonality mitigation through year-round outdoor and wellness travel.[^250]
rewrites.44CFE300: Yet two limits apply. The survey leaves out the domestic market and seven African markets, among them Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana. Its findings are directional rather than definitive. No Western Cape validation exists yet. Stakeholders also name interests outside the four: medical tourism, township culture, eco-adventure and international business events. These are product interests that cut across the segments, not a fifth segment.[^253]
rewrites.35F518BE: Wesgro should market by segment within market and judge results by value as well as volume. The UK and Germany anchor the near term with a combined pool of about 12.5 million. The USA is the largest single pool outside China. The same research that tests the segments here should extend them to the domestic and African markets, which the survey leaves out. The City's framework for 2019 to 2024 set out four segments of its own: Indulgers, Explorers, Specialists and business-events delegates.[^254]
rewrites.6196D738: Two conversion levers join the segment work. The first is urgency. Campaigns carry dated reasons to travel now: events from the green-season calendar, seasonal moments and limited offers (objective 2). The second is reassurance. Market messaging and trade briefings carry current, factual safety information, drawn from the safety workstream in I17 (objective 19). Neither lever needs new product and both can run from the 2027/28 season.
rewrites.16C30FF6: The order matters. Segment targets and validation come first, in 2027, with the brand tests and a baseline of aided and unaided awareness for the city, the province and its regions (I16). The findings are directional. Wesgro should not move the budget on them at scale until they hold for the Western Cape (section 4.3). Spend moves to each segment's own channels from 2028. Spend per visitor joins Wesgro's targets from 2029, once the data exists to track it.
rewrites.57D6E6A9: Test three brand presentations in priority markets (Cape Town as gateway endorsement, a Western Cape umbrella and regional brands leading specialist campaigns) and write regional product, inventory links and completed regional bookings into campaign and airline agreements
rewrites.0C9B3C1A: Segment targeting works because it moves money to where incidence, fit and channel meet. Curious Explorers are 30% of UK and US travellers. The province scores 4.6 out of 5 on its ability to win them. Discerning Connoisseurs book 42% of trips through luxury travel advisors and 6% through OTAs. Broad awareness misses them, while advisor partnerships reach them at the point of sale.[^255]
rewrites.3A5D7242: New Zealand gives each priority market a role, with the USA as its high-yield growth engine. It judges performance on revenue per visitor and length of stay over arrivals. Valencia matches product to purpose in a similar way, with sector-led programmes from gastronomy to business events that attract purpose-driven, higher-value travellers. Its tourist spend rose 21% in 2024 and spending per trip 6.3%, though no source isolates the programmes' share of that rise. The transfer depends on two changes: yield metrics beside the arrivals count and partnerships with specialist distribution networks.[^256]
rewrites.577238E9: The green season is a seat problem and an events problem at once. June holds 6.4% of the year's international seats and business events are the lever best placed to fill the trough, though international meetings now peak from September to November.
rewrites.0DDE7511: Yet the trough is a seat problem as well as a demand problem. Airlines cut seats in the same months that visitors fall away. Connecting traffic is especially critical in the green season. Leisure marketing alone cannot fill a month that carriers have already thinned (section 2.4). The province needs reasons to travel that are fixed in the calendar, booked months ahead and sold with the seats.[^258]
rewrites.2A3DBFE7: Business events are the best of those reasons. They can be scheduled more flexibly than leisure trips, so they can strengthen demand in shoulder and green-season periods. Two gaps remain: aim and measurement. International meetings cluster just after the trough. Only conferences are counted well (section 2.3).[^259]
rewrites.5C6F8C4C: A bid won is not a winter night delivered. Wesgro secured 36 bids in 2024/25 with an estimated value of R745.1 million. The CTICC's forward book lists congresses in May and June 2027 (section 2.3). Forecast value does not show which months the delegates fill. Public event money is also small and tied to other purposes: DEDAT's R7 million Tourism Growth Fund supports attraction and business development, not hosting.
rewrites.30BE356F: June to August and December to January are structurally weak for business events and peak-date constraints lose events
rewrites.7963AD37: DEDAT's R7 million Tourism Growth Fund supports attraction and business development, not event hosting; R4.2 million is earmarked for hallmark and incubator sport events; no South African Formula 1 race is on the 2027 calendar; rights fees and guarantees were not verified
rewrites.3F240892: The CTICC hosted 330 events in the year to June 2025 (63 of them international) and lists congresses for May and June 2027
rewrites.1C2D185D: Source: Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026 (scheduled seats); Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025 (Diag; Wesgro Visitor Tracking Survey 2024); Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026 (DSA); Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026 (SIR). The ICCA months are summed from the printed monthly counts. The 2025 ICCA row of 65 covers Stellenbosch and Cape Town and is not comparable. ICCA counts are revised between editions: the printed series gives 46 meetings for 2023 where Wesgro reported 42 in July 2024. The yearly total of 137 sits one above the 136 monthly records.
rewrites.0AAFE38B: Two limits qualify the numbers. The October to March share is about 62% for 2025, computed from a month-of-travel table whose shares sum to 104.9% and normalised. The only reported split is 61% to 39% for 2024 and this report carries both. Only conferences are measured: meetings are absent from provincial statistics, incentive volumes are unverified and exhibitions are unquantified.[^260]
rewrites.0F2B24D4: Wesgro should build an April to September events spine and sell it with the seats, with May to August as its first winter portfolio. Its plan sets 161 business event bids over FY26 to FY30 and the spine decides when they land. Wesgro organises sales by buyer, because each buys differently: corporate midweek retreats, extensions to congresses already secured, new association bids, incentives with weather-resilient itineraries, exhibitions with non-local buyers and leisure events with non-local attendance. It contracts dated green-season offers for named low-demand weeks with airline and trade partners, with rain alternatives and buyer commitments before any public support. Incentive packages test the cooler season with Indian and Gulf planners.[^261]
rewrites.270D4A8B: Supported offers are judged against a comparison. Each season, Wesgro compares the supported dates and products with similar unsupported ones or phases the offers in. It adjusts the comparison for fares, route changes, school holidays and weather. Offers that deliver additional nights at acceptable public cost are renewed. The longer congress pipeline is kept separate, because it runs on a different clock.
rewrites.64A79ABB: Contract dated green-season offers for named low-demand weeks with airlines and trade, with rain alternatives and buyer commitments before any public support; test cooler-season incentive packages with Indian and Gulf planners
rewrites.4AF342DD: Measure meetings, incentives and exhibitions; build one monthly green-season baseline with accommodation partners: sold and available room nights by region and type, with the shoulder months split from May to August
rewrites.72AEDE6E: Association conferences are won with long lead times and they bring visitors who might not otherwise consider the province. A congress confirmed for July gives carriers a load to plan against. That is the case Wesgro needs to hold winter seats (objective 7). Events used this way sustain year-round tourism demand and air connectivity. They also reach beyond the city. The main event can stay in Cape Town while delegates spend extra nights elsewhere. Stellenbosch and George can host the next phase of regional conferences.[^263]
rewrites.48758A8B: Two further cases test the approach (Appendix A3). Tasmania's Off Season recruits distinctive winter offers ahead of each season. Tasmania's government reported 339,800 May to August visitors in 2025, a result associated with the campaign and not isolated to it. Melbourne shows the fiscal side. Its 2024 Formula 1 race needed A$102.313 million of government investment after revenue, so a gross impact claim cannot stand in for an appraisal at full public cost.
rewrites.17C856BE: **Initiative I2**, green-season events and business-events calendar (section 4.3). **Indicators** T1-05 green-season nights and share at impact level and T2-02 ICCA meetings and T2-03 April to September seat share at outcome level (section 5.2).
rewrites.68D457A9: Travellers who want to visit struggle to find the province beyond Cape Town on the platforms they use: itineraries, transfers, what is open, what is safe and how to buy it. Information and regional content therefore lead. The discovery-to-sale audit is one action among several.
rewrites.20198603: Interest that finds no information is lost. Travellers plan on platforms and each growth market uses its own (section 2.3). Chinese travellers plan on Xiaohongshu and Douyin and book on Trip.com and Fliggy. Indian travellers use Instagram, YouTube and MakeMyTrip. Gulf travellers use Almosafer and private advisors. A region that is absent from those platforms does not exist for the traveller, however good its product is. The open question is how far the province beyond Cape Town reaches them and with what information.[^265]
rewrites.0E36E73A: The gap decides how far growth to 2035 spreads. Cape Town is the gateway. The case for growth beyond the Metro rests on visitors moving out and staying longer. The Overberg says it does not package its offer early enough to be front of mind when travellers book flights. A traveller who cannot see how to reach a region, what is open there or whether it is safe will leave it out of the trip.[^266]
rewrites.6B515025: Booking is one part of the same barrier and it differs by product. A listed business may lack content, live inventory, workable distribution terms or demand. Community guides and some public attractions still lack a first online route. Rural broadband sits outside Wesgro's reach as a national programme.
rewrites.344FB1AC: International flows concentrate on the Cape Peninsula and regional destinations are often left out of itineraries
rewrites.39470C67: About 40% or more of smaller operators are said to lack online booking; the source gives no scope and the audit tests it
rewrites.15C5F0BF: No ranking, travel-date, checkout or sales test has been run; the cases were chosen (not sampled) and exclude informal and community supply
rewrites.00079FAE: The evidence separates three kinds of product. Regional rooms are listed: every eligible case in the desk test had a platform listing, inside the core and outside it. Named attractions outside the core reach the marketplace as stops on Cape Town day tours. None showed a standalone online ticket. Community product still sells by phone or through city operators (section 2.5).
rewrites.3B892121: Elsewhere the product itself is missing: the Overberg and West Coast marine and wildflower assets have no guided tours and no bookable product. What no source measures is the step after listing: whether the product is found, has inventory on the dates travellers want and converts into a sale. The I3 audit measures each step by district, for accommodation and for experiences separately. It sets the baseline for T2-04 (section 5.4).[^267]
rewrites.24C5249F: Listing and recognition work as a pair. A March 2026 platform snapshot shows that short-term rental listings already exist in four regional municipalities (section 2.4), so the audit starts from some stock. A traveller who cannot place the Overberg or the Karoo is less likely to search for either (section 2.3). Yet awareness alone cannot land a regional night where rooms, transport or bookable product are missing. A named stop on a day tour is exposure, not a regional night, so the measure that counts is a completed regional booking. Objective 1 builds the recognition. This objective builds the place for it to land.
rewrites.7AB0A809: Content and the audit both start in 2027. Research builds the inventory with the LTOs (field checks included for informal and community product) and publishes the first presence and exposure baseline for T2-04. A bounded support trial follows in 2028, with a comparison group where feasible. It tracks fulfilled regional nights, paid visits and operators' net receipts after commission. Support scales from 2029 only where the trial paid. Packaged itineraries go onto the chosen platforms in the same period (section 4.3). No provincial marketplace or platform is built before the audit reports. Regional products with confirmed terms keep selling throughout.
rewrites.6FEC64D6: Keep one current source of what is open, how to get there and what is safe in each region; supply it to the trade, the platforms and visitor services
rewrites.337ADB0A: Run a bounded support trial where the audit verifies a failure: a first booking route for unlisted product and, for listed product, content, inventory, distribution terms or packaging, with a comparison group
rewrites.0A7C6A43: Choose platform and trade partners from priority-market journey evidence, starting with the audit's findings on Trip.com, Almosafer and Booking.com; list packaged regional itineraries on them
rewrites.6DF6EA15: Information turns interest the province has already earned into a plan. A booking route turns the plan into payment. The Overberg says potential visitors do not grasp how close the district is to Cape Town. Content, listing and packaging go together. A listing puts outer-district product on the platform where a traveller already plans, but only visible, complete information reaches that traveller at the moment of decision. The audit then shows, district by district, which step fails and whether support moved it.[^269]
rewrites.658B86DA: India and China grow fastest in the base case, at 8% a year to 2035, against 5% for the Middle East and Brazil in their acceleration group. India and China start from a low base, at about 2.6% and 1.4% of South Africa's overseas tourists in September 2025. The upside is large and much of it is already in the air.[^271]
rewrites.258E82EE: Air India and IndiGo have no aircraft to spare before the end of the decade and no South African airline can fly the sector
rewrites.0B55A248: The upside comes in two parts. The hub flow is available now, on routes with spare seats and carriers that gain from every connecting passenger. The direct route is not: the accelerated case depends on confirmed direct routes and without them volume reverts to base. This objective therefore works the hub flow now and builds the route case for later.[^274]
rewrites.669C0B88: The hub work comes first because it needs no new seats. The diagnosis runs beside it in 2027. Wesgro agrees joint market support with the three hub carriers in 2027. Activation on the Chinese and Indian platforms runs in market from 2028 (section 4.3). The direct route cases wait for runway capacity and go to carriers from 2032. Wesgro's plan targets three international tourism marketing campaigns over FY26 to FY30. Any that run in India or China should convert inside the platforms and with the hub carriers.[^277]
rewrites.68171E48: Run a joint route, fare, visa and product diagnosis of the India and China markets with the hub carriers and the trade; test direct services commercially before any route case goes forward
rewrites.1C188F6C: Escalate ETA performance for China and India and the route designation for China that is decided government to government
rewrites.4F426FAA: The mature markets are where the province earns its premium. Its high-spend visitors come from Europe and North America. The mature group grows steadily to 2035, but more slowly than the hub and acceleration markets (section 2.3). Growth here comes from value per visitor more than from volume.[^279]
rewrites.40EE2836: Two things stand in the way: carrier pricing and the province's own measures. On full routes, carriers are expected to raise fares rather than add new services, which frustrates the wish for more visitors. The province must therefore earn more per visitor without losing share. Yet its targets count arrivals. Spend per visitor by market is reported for a single year.[^281]
rewrites.43002949: The top five supplied 63% of overseas arrivals in 2025 and the UK, Germany and USA 52%
rewrites.45748D46: Wesgro should protect share and raise value per visitor in the mature markets and work the full routes for frequency and gauge before it chases new ones. Drawing these visitors beyond the Metro serves the same end while the growth markets develop. There is tactical room for added frequency on some routes and larger aircraft from some airlines.[^283]
rewrites.5B53936D: Length of stay is the second yield lever. About a third of North American, German and French visitors to South Africa travel to more than one province. Most multi-province travellers take in wildlife (section 2.3). Wesgro should sell extensions through the operators who build those itineraries, starting with the US and UK trade. The offer is two or three more nights in the Cape Winelands, on the Whale Coast or on the Garden Route, packaged as an add-on with its transfer (objective 10). Each added night raises spend without an added seat or a peak-hour runway slot.[^284]
rewrites.235C7DC3: The full routes come first. From 2027 Wesgro makes the frequency and gauge case to their carriers, because seats held now protect share until the runway relief arrives (section 4.3). Wesgro agrees the extension strategy with the US and UK trade in 2027 and luxury-advisor distribution follows in 2028. Spend per visitor and length of stay join Wesgro's own targets from 2029, once the data-sharing protocol supplies them (objective 18).
rewrites.113505BA: Add two measures beside arrivals in Wesgro's own targets: spend per visitor by market with length of stay and each market's share of air outbound trips
rewrites.1B33B7E7: Wesgro should run Africa as two markets: a regional volume base held through capacity and value and a premium growth market in Nigeria and Kenya won through conversion. Nigeria is the priority for luxury, status-driven and conference travel. Kenya is the priority for business mobility and premium urban breaks. Both are reached through premium activation and the trade.[^291]
rewrites.1D920C48: Convert rest-of-Africa travellers who stop in Johannesburg with onward packages and give regional delegates leisure extensions
rewrites.7C859683: Escalate visas for African markets (building on the Ghana visa waiver of November 2023) and liberalisation of regional air routes
